artifact_note: Built from this tree with its own build-dist-zip.sh, which fails closed: .distignore plus a hard deny list, then a scan of the staged tree that refuses to write the zip if a forbidden path survived. sha256 in SHA256SUMS.

assembled_from.codex-gpt5: full profile every turn, RAG fallthrough, get_response_result(), personality boilerplate removal, genome/profile fingerprint
assembled_from.opencode-big-pickle: no-hedge method pair and the method_exists guards
assembled_from.grok-4-6: public request protection, IVR greeting variables, line-break forms, Public Title placement

verification.wordpress_plugin_check: The one warning naming a defect (WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.InterpolatedNotPrepared) was repaired in v5. A full WordPress-standard PHPCS scan reports no security-, escaping-, sanitisation-, nonce- or prepared-SQL findings.
verification.journey_harness: DEFERRED — needs WP-CLI on the target site
verification.contract_acceptance: DEFERRED — personality built from scratch, attached to a pack, carrying that flow to its outcome

v3_fixes: Recovered answer no longer shown twice after a signed-in reload mid-response.
profile_hash computed on read when the stored field is empty, so the chat log column is never blank.
Chat log export filename carries a full MTS to the millisecond instead of the date alone.
v4_fixes: The framework no longer claims membership grants 'full access to all content'.
A personality built in the builder opens with the same header the shipped ones do.
The portability line moved to the download; provenance is visible beside the profile.
The site index reads whichever post types the flow selects, not only 'post'.
BuddyBoss group directory indexed, catalogued on every turn, and fail-closed by tier and group privacy.
The compiled profile is sent on every turn, not only the first. Recorded here after the fact: it shipped in v4 and was first written up in v5.
plugin_check_ai_provider_note: Plugin Check suggests WordPress 7.0 wp_ai_client_prompt() wherever it sees a provider hostname. The five flagged lines are the model-catalog and model-detail endpoints, which enumerate what a floscAdmin key can use so the admin dropdown shows real models. The AI Client sends prompts; it does not list a provider catalogue for a key, so the suggested replacement does not cover these calls. Left visible rather than annotated away. Adopting the AI Client for the prompt path is a real feature decision, not a lint fix.
v5_fixes: A personality can be renamed. state.soul.name was read in six places in the builder — the profile heading, the identity line, the save payload and four export filenames — and written in none. No field existed, so the name seeded from the library at boot was the only name a personality could ever have. Same for the role. The id is untouched: it is the key a flow attaches by.

The chat logger quotes its table name with a %i placeholder instead of interpolating it into the SQL string (Plugin Check, WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.InterpolatedNotPrepared), and check_log_contract.php now fails on any line that interpolates it.
v6_fixes: user_tier column: the VGM tier FLOSC computed on every turn and never wrote down. A Guest and a Member were indistinguishable in the chat log, so "is anyone registering repeatedly to farm Guest content?" had no column to ask.

provider_request_id column: the id the provider returns, captured through an http_response filter so it covers all four providers rather than only the one FLOSC calls directly. Stored, never sent. It is the only identifier that exists on both sides of the wire.

FLOSC now identifies itself to AI providers: a User-Agent and one X-DA1-Trace header carrying install, site, flow, personality, knowledge base, tier and message pair. Flow, personality and knowledge base ride as per-install HMACs. Nothing identifying an individual visitor. Both switchable in Settings, disclosed in readme.txt External Services, and FLOSC phones nothing home.
The follow-up chatpack no longer tells the model a buyer has "full access" — v4 fixed the phase list and missed the state-update line. Two chatpack sections both numbered 5c are now 5c and 5d.
A profile can be given a filename. The five downloads named themselves five different ways, one with two dots; they now share one fileBase() and underscores throughout.
Profiles open with "# DA1/FLOSC AI Personality Profile Name: <name>", byte-identical across the builder and all four shipped personalities.

The download footer is rewritten: density bands, both hashes named apart, and the chain from the file to the turns it produced to the provider’s record of each call. The About block moves to the top of the design copy, and workshop.json carries the same facts as real JSON keys.
Optional source_site line in downloads, off by default.
Seven Trajectory wellsprings in the aspect palette, each carrying a literal {url} placeholder, gated so none can ship a real address.
BubblyBetty no longer describes herself with an idiom built on having legs.
v7_fixes: v6 hung the AI tab. profileFooter() read the builder state hash off fullSpec(), and the new provenance block in workshopFile() called profileFooter()'s row builder — closing fullSpec() -> workshopFile() -> provenanceRows() -> fullSpec(). renderOut() enters that chain on every redraw and each turn rebuilt the whole workshop object, so the page died before the stack overflowed. No console error; node --check parses it fine.

provenanceRows() now computes the hash itself rather than reading it back off a caller. check_builder_cycles.php parses the builder's functions, builds a call graph over the eleven that produce a document, and fails on any route back to where it started.

From Grok's independent diagnosis, which found the same loop by a different route: builder_state_hash is now guarded, not only wrapped. hashText('') returns 811c9dc5, the FNV offset basis — a real-looking fingerprint for a profile with nothing in it. No profile, no fingerprint.
